picks.excerpt: Microsoft's experimental Intelligent Terminal for Windows isn't locked to Copilot — the writer got it running a local LLM in five minutes, and it also supports Claude Code, OpenAI Codex and Gemini agents, pointing at agentic, on-device AI on the desktop.
picks.rationale: Highest actionability — an open, agent-agnostic terminal running local LLMs plus Claude Code/Codex/Gemini directly reshapes a designer-developer's daily desktop workflow.

picks.excerpt: HMD's new retro Nokia feature phones (200/210/215/235 4G) add a dedicated AI button on the D-pad that summons an on-device Sikey AI assistant for voice queries, alarms, reminders and camera control — free for 180 days, then a small annual fee.
picks.rationale: Novel form-factor story — a dedicated hardware AI button on sub-$50 feature phones signals on-device assistants going mainstream far beyond flagship smartphones.

picks.excerpt: Leaked images of Insta360's upcoming X6 show a more compact, GoPro-like action cam with 8K 360-degree capture and the company's AI subject tracking and reframing, expected to start around $800 as GoPro struggles.
picks.rationale: Freshest item and concrete AI-camera hardware — 8K 360 capture with AI reframing is directly relevant to creators shooting reference and content.

picks.excerpt: OpenAI teamed with Work Louder on a Codex-branded macro pad — an illuminated hardware device that turns Codex AI-agent commands into physical button presses, OpenAI's first tangible dev-focused gadget.
picks.rationale: Chosen over the 9to5Mac teaser as the more concrete product piece for the same Codex-hardware cluster — a shipping macro pad mapping AI-agent commands to physical keys.
